entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Gnaeus Manlius Vulso (Gnaeus Manlius Vulso) was a Roman consul for the year 189 BC, leading a victorious campaign against the Galatian Gauls of Asia Minor in 189 BC during the Galatian War. He was awarded a triumph in 187 BC.




Gnaeus Manlius Vulso was a prominent figure in Roman history, known for his military prowess and political influence. As a consul, he played a key role in shaping Roman policy and expanding Roman territories. His leadership during the Galatian War marked a significant turning point in Roman history, as it showcased Roman military power and strategic thinking.





The legacy of Gnaeus Manlius Vulso extends beyond his own lifetime, as his actions and decisions had a lasting impact on Roman society and politics. His triumph in 187 BC was a testament to his success and a symbol of Roman power, inspiring future generations of Roman leaders.




A striking statistic is that Gnaeus Manlius Vulso's military campaigns resulted in the capture of over 100,000 Galatian prisoners, demonstrating the scale of Roman military power at the time.
